title: Compile candidates: fiction and film
description: Rufus's point: fiction and film may be better teaching examples than real cases, because a collective action problem has to be felt before the 2x2 means anything. Cover: films and novels whose plot IS a collective action structure — holdouts, betrayals under interrogation, commons collapse, arms races, defection under pressure, the group that holds and the group that doesn't. Include the obvious (If a Tree Falls is already prep viewing) and the non-obvious. Note clip length and where the mechanism is visible on screen. Westerns, war films, heist films, courtroom films and disaster films are unusually rich; so are epics where the line holds or breaks.
acceptance_criteria: 20-25 candidates at course/research/examples-fiction.md. Each says what structure the plot instantiates, which module it serves, the specific scene and roughly how long it runs, and whether the clip stands alone without the film's context.
notes: 28 candidates grouped by structure not genre. Standalone-best clips: Dr Strangelove War Room (characters explain commitment-device theory out loud — highest value for the Schelling module), The Dark Knight ferries (antagonist states the payoff matrix), Norma Rae UNION sign (threshold cascade rendered in sound, and the list's cleanest success). Weak fits flagged honestly: Jaws has no defection in it; Dark Knight is closer to mutual deterrence than strict PD; Do the Right Thing doesn't travel as a clip; Spartacus scene has no basis in Appian or Plutarch. Four entries (Thucydides, Xenophon, Things Fall Apart, The Plague) marked prep reading, no footage. Thin structures noted: commons collapse as plot (fiction wants a villain, a commons failure has none) and coordination without communication.

title: Compile candidates: warfare and what makes groups hold
description: The biggest gap in the current set. Existing lists cover cooperation DESPITE war (trench truces, Christmas truce, Danish rescue, Le Chambon) but nothing on what makes a fighting group cohere — which is the positive case Rufus wants. Cover: the hoplite phalanx and why the line holds; Marathon, Thermopylae, Plataea; Socrates in the line at Potidaea and Delium; Roman legion cohesion and decimation as punishment; small-unit bonding and the modern literature on why men fight (Marshall's contested fire-ratio claim, Shils and Janowitz on primary groups, Grossman); mutiny and rout as the failure mode; conscription and free riding; mercenary and citizen armies compared. Both faces: cohesion achieved, and cowardice and breakdown.
acceptance_criteria: 20-25 candidates at course/research/examples-warfare.md in the established entry format. Each names the mechanism holding the group together, not just the outcome. Contested claims flagged — Marshall's fire ratio especially.

title: Spawn per-example research and media beads from the selection
description: For each selected example: a research bead, with a media child for clips, images and primary sources. Media nests under its example, never standalone. If the hunt turns up strong media for something not on the list, create a new candidate bead linked discovered-from.

title: SELECT: cut the candidate lists to a working set
description: Rufus's call, not an agent's. REVIEW HERE: course/research/index.md — one line per candidate across all lists, with flags for contested accounts [C], known media [M] and unverified details [?]. Links through to the full entry. Read that, mark the ones you want, and the marked set becomes the working set. Only then do per-example research and media beads get created — media cannot be scoped before the examples exist.
acceptance_criteria: A selected list exists. Per-example research beads created, each with a media child.

title: Compile candidates: contemporary cases
description: AI arms race, climate, nuclear and bioweapons, fisheries, antibiotics, information commons, attention. The ones that connect the theory to what people are actually working on.
acceptance_criteria: A candidate list of 20-25 entries at course/research/examples-*.md, each with: what happened, why it is a collective action case, which module(s) it could serve, whether media exists, and a real source. Deliberately more candidates than will be used. Working material, not wiki content.
notes: 29 candidates, each running the five diagnostic questions plus a substitutes line. Key finding: Montreal vs Kyoto only teaches as a diagnostic result, not a template — Barrett and Sunstein both treat Montreal as an easy case. Three additions strengthen the module: Kigali (a climate agreement that worked because it was shaped like an ozone agreement, cutting off 'climate is intrinsically harder'), leaded petrol (global phase-out with no treaty at all, isolating substitutes as the operative variable), CFC-11 2013-19 (defection detected from the atmosphere rather than reporting). Gaps: almost no non-Western cases (ASEAN haze, Nile Basin), nothing at intermediate scale between Wikipedia and global treaties.

title: Compile candidates: non-human cooperation
description: Animal and other non-human cases, for the cooperative ape module and for showing cooperation is not a human invention. Prioritise cases with good footage.
acceptance_criteria: A candidate list of 20-25 entries at course/research/examples-*.md, each with: what happened, why it is a collective action case, which module(s) it could serve, whether media exists, and a real source. Deliberately more candidates than will be used. Working material, not wiki content.
notes: 25 candidates, footage graded Poor/Moderate/Good/Excellent rather than uniformly claimed. 9 entries are cooperation failing or being cheated (drongo false alarms, cleaner wrasse biting, Dictyostelium/Myxococcus/Pseudomonas cheats, worker-laid eggs, acacia parasite, lion laggards). Disputes flagged: meerkat sentinels probably not altruistic (Clutton-Brock 1999), vampire bat reciprocity contested against kin selection, chimp role-taking unresolved, wolf teamwork reproducible from 2 rules with no communication. Rejected a widely-repeated musk ox formation-time statistic as content-farm sourced, and recorded the rejection in the file.
